A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated introduction material and renumbered appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original OpenWebText training comparisons, sampling experiments, and numerical-precision ablations, including perplexity, entropy, and runtime results in Sections 5–6 and Appendix I.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Sections 5–6 and the renamed Appendix J.

M1.justification: The training objectives, first-hitting sampler, and parallel and higher-order procedures remain unchanged. The masked-ratio conditioning highlighted in v4 Section 3.1 was already documented in v3 Appendix I.1.1.

E1.justification: Empirical coverage remains OpenWebText language modeling and text generation. The new DiffSound example in Appendix J.3 illustrates computational costs without reporting an additional audio dataset evaluation.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain AR, SEDD Absorb, MDLM with and without caching, and the same sampler variants. DiffSound appears as an illustrative timing configuration, not an additional generation-quality baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix J.3 adds a matched-NFE analytical timing comparison with explicit model, vocabulary, sequence-length, and sampling-step assumptions. The experimental protocols in Appendix H remain unchanged; the added analysis does not establish that benchmarks were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix J.3 analyzes how speedup depends on model size, vocabulary, sequence length, and sampling budget. Existing training, temperature, precision, and higher-order sampler ablations are retained. Figure 15 is an explanatory schematic, not a new experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates. Existing sample averaging and point-estimate reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing experimental table values, plotted results, and generated-text examples are unchanged. Appendix J.3 adds calculated speedups of approximately 17× at 10,000 steps, 5× at 2,048 steps, and 1.07× for its DiffSound configuration; these are analytical estimates rather than improved benchmark measurements.

T1.justification: Appendix J.3 introduces an additive runtime model, NFE × t1 + NCS × t2, and derives a speedup ratio at matched NFE. The existing ELBO, first-hitting-time, truncated-Gumbel, and caching results and proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and central equivalence, sampling, and numerical-precision claims are retained. The introduction and conclusion add broader recommendations to reconsider investment in MDMs and prefer simpler masked models, extending the earlier skepticism about text-generation superiority.

C2.justification: Appendix J.2.2 strengthens the explanation that accumulated prioritized unmasking drives diversity loss. Section 6.1 and Appendix J.3 explicitly qualify the 20× speedup as setting-dependent. The conclusion adds broader concerns about discrete diffusion while retaining the text-order limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix J.3 newly supplies runtime-component ratios and model/configuration assumptions. Its paper-case figures of approximately 600M parameters and 50,526 vocabulary entries are not reconciled with Appendix H.2's retained 170M and 50,257 figures. Existing hardware, training details, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Yang et al. (2023), DiffSound, for the timing example and sharpens the existing critical positioning toward MDM research. The detailed related-work discussion in Appendix B and the principal novelty attributions remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction is rewritten around numbered findings, with its earlier contribution summary preserved in new Appendix I. Additional Results becomes Appendix J, and localized explanatory and limitations passages are added. Most sections and technical prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figure 15 illustrating prioritized unmasking, resizes Figure 7, moves Table 2, and relocates several appendix plots. Existing plotted content is preserved, and generated-text examples are renumbered without replacement.

improvement.justification: The added mechanism illustration and conditional speedup analysis improve explanation. However, Appendix J.3's paper-case assumptions are unreconciled with Appendix H.2, weakening confidence in the new timing estimates. The introduction and conclusion also broaden criticism beyond the unchanged text-only experiments. These explanatory gains and reliability concerns leave the net quality change uncertain.
